title: Replace hook-based interaction runtime with a functional JS controller (S2)

complexity.rationale: Substantial remaining implementation work where each subsystem being ported — popover/inspect dialogs, click/hover detection, legend interaction, hover animation — requires its own new, non-precedented design rather than repeating an existing pattern, plus real coordination risk with the separately in-progress dataNavigatorManual accessibility work touching the same files. Phase 1 (mount/resize/destroy) and Phase 2 (click/legend) are complete and de-risked; later phases (popover/inspect content mounting, debug-event pub-sub) are only specified at the original end-state level, not yet designed against current code the way Phases 1-2 were.

summary: Replace the React-hooks-driven interaction/rendering runtime in react-spectrum-charts-s2 (Chart.tsx, RscChart.tsx, VegaChart.tsx, and their supporting hooks/utils) with a functional JS/TS controller — a factory function returning a plain object of closures, not a class — that owns vega-embed mounting, resize, click/hover detection, and popover/inspect state via explicit calls instead of React effect-dependency wiring. This matches the pattern already established in this codebase's own in-progress accessibility work (the dataNavigatorManual branch's `attachDataNavigator`), not a novel convention. The public JSX authoring API and vega-spec-builder-s2 are completely unchanged — this is purely an internal runtime replacement. Motivated by real, already-experienced fragility in the current hook tangle (in particular VegaChart.tsx's embed-effect-vs-resize-effect separation, a classic dependency-array footgun) and a confirmed latent async-lifecycle race under React Strict Mode, not by bundle size. Enabling a future server-built-spec (RSC) rendering path is a natural side benefit of the resulting data-driven design, not the primary motivation. Being implemented incrementally: Phase 1 (mount/resize/destroy + both confirmed bugs) is done and verified; Phase 2 (click detection + legend interaction, including the hidden-series live-signal fix) is done and verified; later phases remain at original-filing detail only.
requirements: The public component tree, props, and TypeScript types (Chart, Axis, Line, Legend, ChartPopover, ChartInspect, and every other existing mark/child component) are unchanged — no breaking change for consumers.
childrenAdapter (JSX → ChartOptions) and vega-spec-builder-s2's buildSpec() are not modified by this work; the spec produced for a given chart is byte-for-byte the same as today.

The interactive runtime — mount/update/resize/destroy, click/hover detection, popover/inspect open-close, legend hover-highlight and click-to-hide, hover animation, controlled highlight — is reimplemented as a single functional controller: one factory function returning a plain object of methods built via closures over private state, not an ES6 class and not several composed stateful sub-controllers. This follows the existing `attachDataNavigator`-style pattern already used in this codebase (see dataNavigatorManual branch) rather than introducing a new architectural convention.

The controller exposes 'cheap resize' and 'expensive spec/view recreation' as two explicit, separately-invokable operations, mirroring today's VegaChart embed-effect vs. resize-effect split, so a container resize can never trigger a full view recreation (or vice versa) by accident.

The controller's mount function guards against the async embed()-then-cleanup race confirmed during spec review: today's VegaChart.tsx calls embed() (async) and sets chartView.current inside .then(), but its effect cleanup checks chartView.current synchronously — under React Strict Mode's double-invoke, the first embed() call's promise hasn't resolved when cleanup runs, so cleanup no-ops and a second embed() call fires, risking two Views mounting. The new controller's construct function must use a cancellation flag captured at call time, checked inside the embed().then() callback before touching any state or calling onNewView, so a superseded async mount cleanly finalizes itself instead of leaking. IMPLEMENTED (Phase 1): a generation counter + destroyed flag do double duty for this and for the AN-445759 zero-dimensions case; regression-proven by reverting the guard, confirming the new tests fail, and restoring it.

Separately from the async-mount race above: today's VegaChart.tsx registers rscContainerWidth via vega's expressionFunction() at module load time, which throws under Next.js (or any framework's) SSR pass of a "use client" component ('Unrecognized function' / expressionFunction is not a function, confirmed during the earlier RSC investigation this project grew out of). Since attachVegaChartController.ts becomes the new home for this registration, it must guard it (e.g. typeof window !== 'undefined', or register lazily on first construct rather than at module scope) from the start, rather than patching the soon-to-be-deleted VegaChart.tsx module-scope call first and redoing it here. IMPLEMENTED (Phase 1): guarded with typeof window !== 'undefined'; corresponding bug spec (vegachart-ssr-expressionfunction-crash) marked implemented and moved to issues/implemented/.

Arbitrary user-authored JSX content inside ChartPopover/ChartInspect continues to render correctly; the controller imperatively mounts/unmounts a React root for this content only, keyed to the relevant mark's open/close state. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — later phase, not yet designed against current code.
The public imperative handle (ChartHandle, used for export/copy today) continues to expose the live Vega View, now sourced from the controller. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — later phase.

Existing signal-based interactivity (hover animation, controlled highlight, legend highlight, tooltip/popover voronoi wiring) produces behaviorally identical Vega signal reads/writes to today — same signal names, same symmetric set/clear discipline documented in the architecture docs. One confirmed exception, fixed rather than merely replicated: legend hidden-series toggling currently forces a full view recreation (React useState → new signals object → VegaChart's recreate effect → full destroy+embed) instead of a cheap live signal write — this is a genuine, confirmed inefficiency in the current implementation, not a deliberate design. Phase 2 fixes it: the live Vega hiddenSeries signal becomes the single source of truth (read and written directly via a new controller setSignal method), and useLegend.tsx's useState is removed rather than ported as-is. IMPLEMENTED (Phase 2) and regression-proven: reverting setSignal's toggle-write path and the recreate() carry-forward/defaultHiddenSeries-fallback logic each independently made their new tests fail as expected.

The controller exposes a `getView(): View | undefined` accessor with the same shape RscChart.tsx currently provides to the in-progress `Navigator` component (dataNavigatorManual branch: packages/react-spectrum-charts-s2/src/dataNavigator/Navigator.tsx), and preserves a compatible positioned-container ref, so that separate accessibility effort is not blocked by or required to be redone as part of this refactor. This spec does not itself implement keyboard-navigation accessibility. IMPLEMENTED (Phase 1): getView() exists on the controller handle today. Phase 2 touched RscChart.tsx (interactionConfig wiring) but did not touch the chartView ref/context shape itself, so the Navigator-compatibility integration point is unchanged and still not yet exercised — dataNavigatorManual still does not exist on this branch (confirmed via git ls-tree, only on origin/dataNavigatorManual).

Because closures hide internal state by default (a console.log of the returned handle shows only its methods — {resize: ƒ, updateSpec: ƒ, getView: ƒ, destroy: ƒ} — not the current view/spec/popover state), the controller does not rely on incidental object/closure inspection for debugging. Internal functions are named function declarations, not anonymous arrows, so stack traces remain readable. IMPLEMENTED (Phase 1) for the functions that exist today.

The controller exposes a tiny internal debug-event pub-sub — onDebugEvent(listener) — firing a structured event on every meaningful transition: mount, resize, signal write, popover/inspect open-close, legend toggle. This follows the pattern both TanStack Query's devtools (subscribing to QueryCache/MutationCache events) and XState's inspector (inspector.event()/inspector.snapshot()) independently converged on: expose state *changes* via events for anything to subscribe to, rather than exposing current state via inspection. debugLog() (existing useDebugSpec.tsx convention) becomes just one subscriber, not a special case — this is also the foundation a future visual debug overlay (see the separate floating-debug-overlay spec) subscribes to, without requiring any rework of the controller itself. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — Phase 1's actual attachVegaChartController.ts does not yet have onDebugEvent/getDebugHistory/debugEvents.ts; this remains at original-filing detail only, deferred until a phase actually needs it (the floating-debug-overlay spec's primary Signals/Data/Logs tabs turned out not to depend on this after all — they only need getView() against a live View, which already exists).

The controller maintains a bounded ring buffer (e.g. last 200 events) of its own debug-event stream, retrievable via getDebugHistory(), so 'what led up to this' is answerable after the fact even if the console wasn't open when it happened — a lightweight analog of the Vega Editor's signal timeline/replay feature. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — see above.

When debug is enabled, the controller bumps Vega's own log level (vega.Warn default → vega.Debug) so Vega's internal dataflow evaluation logging surfaces alongside the controller's own events, and exposes getView()._runtime (Vega's documented-but-unofficial live dataflow-operator-graph accessor) for advanced inspection — read-only, never mutated internally. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.
All debug console output (debugLog calls, Vega's own logger) is tagged/grouped by the chart's existing chartId so multi-chart pages don't produce interleaved, ambiguous output. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.

When debug is enabled, the controller favors surfacing an explicit path to open the current spec in the Vega Editor (vega-embed's existing 'actions' menu already supports this) rather than requiring actions: true unconditionally just to get it — the Vega Editor's own signal timeline, annotated visualization, and live data tables are more capable than anything worth reimplementing here. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.

Migration is incremental and validated against the existing test suite at each stage, not a single big-bang replacement. Actual sequencing that emerged (more granular than the original 'resize + basic click first' framing): Phase 1 = mount/destroy/resize/recreate lifecycle + both confirmed bugs (DONE). Phase 2 = click detection + legend interaction, including fixing the hidden-series full-recreate inefficiency (DONE — full monorepo test suite green, 3948 tests). Phase 3+ = popover/inspect content mounting, debug-event pub-sub (NOT YET DESIGNED against current code).
S1 (react-spectrum-charts) is explicitly and permanently out of scope — not a deferred decision. No equivalent redesign is planned for S1's separate interaction-layer implementation.

(Phase 2) Config describing which marks have click/mouseover/contextmenu/axis-label-click behavior continues to be derived from walking sanitizedChildren (JSX), exactly as today's useMarkOnClickDetails/useMarkMouseInputDetails/useAxisLabelOnClickDetails hooks already do — confirmed during Phase 2 design that vega-spec-builder-s2's spec-level usermeta.interactiveMarks metadata is NOT a viable alternative source: it exists purely for spec-build-time visual-encoding purposes (legend highlight config, axis-label dimming opacity rules), is consumed by nothing at runtime today, and structurally cannot carry live callback function references regardless of which marks it lists. This config is passed into the controller as an explicit, plain-data `interactionConfig` object built in React (from JSX), not derived by the controller from the spec. IMPLEMENTED (Phase 2).

(Phase 2) Click-triggered popover opening continues to use the existing DOM hidden-button-click bridge (triggerPopover: document.querySelector('#{chartId}...#{itemName}-popover-button')?.click()) rather than a new React-callback mechanism — confirmed this bridge has zero dependency on React refs/callback props/component identity beyond a stable DOM id convention, so the controller can own full click resolution (including triggering popover opens) while ChartDialog/popover rendering itself remains untouched React code until a later phase. IMPLEMENTED (Phase 2).

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Controller mounts without throwing and matches today's empty-state rendering; no change to EmptyState/LoadingState behavior.

edgeCases.case: Rapid/continuous container resize (e.g. dragging a split pane)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Only the cheap resize path runs per resize event — no view recreation, no flicker, no dropped or out-of-order resize calls under fast repeated events. VERIFIED (Phase 1).

Legend hover-highlight and click-to-hide-series scale correctly and remain responsive with a large number of series, matching current signal-write behavior — and, per Phase 2's design, without forcing a full view recreation per toggle the way today's implementation does. IMPLEMENTED (Phase 2): toggling now writes the live hiddenSeries signal via setSignal() with no recreate.

edgeCases.case: Truncated/long axis labels with click or inspect interaction
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Axis label click and ChartInspect hover behavior (ported from useAxisLabelOnClickDetails/useChartInspectInteractions) is unchanged for truncated labels.

edgeCases.case: Multiple marks with popovers on one chart
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Clicking one mark's interactive overlay opens only that mark's popover content, with no cross-talk — replaces today's COMPONENT_NAME datum-matching with a direct markName → content-renderer lookup in the controller.
Popover/inspect dialog styling (via @react-spectrum/s2's Provider colorScheme) renders correctly despite being mounted imperatively rather than as part of the React children tree.
Permanently out of scope — confirmed, not a deferred question. S1 keeps its own separate, independently-maintained interaction-layer implementation indefinitely.

Not implemented by this spec. The controller must preserve the getView()/container integration point the in-progress Navigator component depends on, so that separate, already-real (tested, dependent on the published data-navigator package) effort keeps working once this refactor lands. Currently Bar-only on that branch; also involves spec-level focus-ring changes in vega-spec-builder-s2's bar builder that are outside this spec's scope entirely.

edgeCases.case: Popover open + hover state interaction conflict
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: An open popover suppresses/interacts with hover-driven opacity changes the same way it does today (see hasPopover-gated opacity rules in the current mark builders) — the controller must reproduce this precedence, not just the individual behaviors in isolation.

edgeCases.case: React 18 Strict Mode double-invocation in development
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Controller construct/destroy lifecycle tolerates Strict Mode's intentional double-invoke without double-mounting vega-embed or leaking listeners, via the cancellation-flag guard described in requirements. Confirmed as a real, currently-latent race in today's implementation, not a hypothetical. VERIFIED (Phase 1): regression-proven by reverting the guard, confirming the new tests fail, restoring it.

edgeCases.case: (Phase 2) Legend hidden-series toggle immediately followed by an unrelated recreate (e.g. a data prop change) before the toggle's view is replaced
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The outgoing view's live hiddenSeries value is captured and carried forward into the new spec's signal patch before the old view is finalized, so the toggle isn't silently lost. This is new behavior (today's toggle always forces its own recreate, so this interleaving can't currently happen) — needs explicit test coverage, not just faithful porting. IMPLEMENTED (Phase 2), regression-proven by reverting the carry-forward read and confirming the new test fails.

edgeCases.case: (Phase 2, discovered during implementation — not anticipated in the original design) Any parent re-render of RscChart that doesn't change the interaction config's actual contents (e.g. an unrelated popover open/close toggling isPopoverOpen context state)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Must not trigger a full VegaChart view recreation. Root cause found via two pre-existing regression tests (AxisThumbnail's 'popover flicker regression' and ChartPopover's fade-on-select test) failing once interactionConfig was wired into VegaChart's recreate-effect dependency array: useLegend.tsx returned a fresh, unmemoized object literal on every call (unlike every sibling detail hook — useMarkOnClickDetails/useMarkMouseInputDetails/useAxisLabelOnClickDetails — which all wrap their return in useMemo), so useChartInteractions's interactionConfig useMemo (which depends on `legend`) recomputed on every render, changing interactionConfig's identity and re-triggering VegaChart's recreate effect. Fixed by memoizing useLegend's return on the legend element's identity. Regression-proven: reverting the memoization reproduces both original test failures; restoring it fixes them.

crossCutting.notes: touchesHoverAnimation/touchesControlledHighlight/touchesLegendInteraction/touchesTooltipOrPopover are all true because this feature's entire purpose is reimplementing the client-side wiring for each of these systems (signal reads/writes, voronoi hover overlay, COMPONENT_NAME popover matching, legendHighlightSignals) in the new controller — no new signals or scales are introduced, and the underlying spec (produced by vega-spec-builder-s2, unmodified by this feature) already defines all of them; only which layer of client code reads/writes them changes. touchesLegendInteraction specifically now also covers a mechanism change, not just a relocation: Phase 2 makes the live hiddenSeries Vega signal the source of truth instead of React useState, confirmed necessary because today's useState-based toggle forces a full view recreation on every click (a real, confirmed inefficiency, verified via code trace: useLegend's setLegendHiddenSeries -> useChartInteractions's memoized signals object -> VegaChart's recreate-effect dependency array -> attachVegaChartController's full destroy+embed). IMPLEMENTED (Phase 2) and regression-proven (see requirements/edgeCases entries for both the hiddenSeries carry-forward/fallback logic and the useLegend memoization fix). requiresNewSignalOrScale stays false — no new signal name is introduced, hiddenSeries already exists; only how it's written changes. requiresS1S2Parity is false because that flag specifically covers mirrored vega-spec-builder <-> vega-spec-builder-s2 files, and this feature touches neither spec-builder package — it's entirely within the react-spectrum-charts-s2 React/runtime layer. S1's react-spectrum-charts package has its own separate, independently-maintained interaction-layer implementation; confirmed during review that it will never receive this redesign — permanently out of scope, not a deferred question.
